title: He looked alive…
paragraphs:
He looked alive…
but heaven called him empty.
Because this wasn’t just a tree.

And if you don’t see yourself in it—
you might be missing the warning.
From a distance, it looked like life.

Like growth.
Like blessing.
Like something worth approaching.
But Jesus didn’t stop at appearances.
Because when Jesus Christ reached the branches…
No evidence of life beneath the surface.
And in one moment that shakes comfortable Christianity…
“May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” — Mark 11:14
Because some of us have mastered looking alive.
We know how to raise our hands in worship…
…but not how to surrender our hearts in private.
We know how to post Scriptures…
…but not how to obey them when it costs us.
We know how to say “God is good”…
…but still bow to secret sin when no one is watching.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because the fig tree wasn’t pretending to be a tree.
But it was failing its purpose.
It had the appearance of fruitfulness…

Looking close to God…
without actually being transformed by Him.
You can sit in church every Sunday…
and still be far from God.
You can know every worship song…
and still not know His voice.
and still be hiding addiction, pride, bitterness, lust.
But heaven is looking for fruit.
“Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.” — Matthew 7:19
God is not looking for flawless people.
And fruit doesn’t come from effort alone.
“I am the vine; you are the branches… apart from Me you can do nothing.” — John 15:5
The fig tree didn’t lack effort.
And sin does that to us.
It disconnects us from the source.
It lets us build an image…
The pride you’ve disguised as confidence.
The compromise you’ve justified as “just this once.”
The double life you’ve learned to manage.
“The fruit of the Spirit is…” — Galatians 5:22–23
Is that what your life produces…
from maintaining an image that doesn’t match your reality?
Because the story doesn’t end in judgment.
That same Jesus who cursed the tree…
“Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us…” — Galatians 3:13
The withering that should have been yours…
He took into His own body.
Because He wasn’t after destroying you.
Not trying harder to grow fruit.
It’s dying to the fake life…
so you can receive a real one.
But you can receive new life.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
Stop hiding behind spiritual language while your soul is starving.

“Lord, I’ve been living on leaves.
I want real life.”
And receive what you cannot earn:

Because the same voice that said,
“Let no fruit grow…”
Is the same voice that says,
“Come to Me… and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28
He is not waiting to destroy you.
If this pierced you—even a little—
And if this stirred something deeper—
If you’re tired of surface-level faith…
If you’re ready for real transformation—
For a voice that keeps pointing you back to Jesus.
Because God is not done speaking.
And your story is not finished.
